title: Which windows share the change?
hook: Slide one pair of coefficients across four inputs.

knows: a weighted sum multiplies inputs by coefficients
doesNotKnow: how the same filter coefficients are reused across positions
why a zero input can preserve an output after a coefficient change

misconception: Every location requires its own independent coefficients, and changing a shared coefficient must change every output.
objective: Recognize reuse of the same two coefficients across valid 1D cross-correlation windows.

claims.text: The input is [1,2,0,1], filter [1,−1], stride 1, valid windows only, no bias, cross-correlation convention; outputs are [−1,2,−1].
claims.source: Independent derivation and source audit: company/reviews/convolution-weight-sharing/2026-10-19-fact-all-ai-foundations.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/pytorch/main/torch/nn/modules/conv.py (Conv1d docstring lines 212–235, valid padding lines 252–255); src/demos/ai/convolution-weight-sharing/model.ts and Demo.tsx. Registered recall verified separately; shared footer coverage gap remains.

claims.text: Changing the shared first coefficient to 2 gives [0,4,−1]. All windows reuse it, but the last first input is zero so that output stays −1. This 1D analogue does not train filters or demonstrate image recognition.

recall.question: A shared first coefficient multiplies inputs 2,0,3 across three windows. Does changing it necessarily change every output?
options: No: the zero contributes no change
No: only the first window uses it
recall.why: Every window uses it, but multiplication by zero can leave an output unchanged.
